Please review the following manuscript. I've poured years of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b02/review-experiment-s235dvs_/call-c00313c5cd344e11836b8bedae7d0f06/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -l manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL']:
 print(name,importlib.util.find_spec(name))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r = PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES', len(r.pages))
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 t=p.extract_text()
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
 print(f'PAGE {i}: {len(t)} chars')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i} ===\\n'+p.extract_text() for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1)))
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"
/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-09.txt tmp/pdfs/page-10.txt tmp/pdfs/page-11.txt tmp/pdfs/page-12.txt tmp/pdfs/page-13.txt tmp/pdfs/page-14.txt'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
shutil.rmtree('tmp/pdfs')
p = Path('tmp')
if not any(p.iterdir()):
 p.rmdir()
print('Removed temporary PDF inspection files; manuscript unchanged.')
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant NLP evaluation problem: how researchers’ collaboration arrangements affect interactive qualitative coding. Its focus on actual research workflows gives the contribution practical value.

The study examines three substantially different approaches on a common dataset of approximately 85,000 tweets, using 20 participants across 15 experiments. Shared initialization within each tool provides a useful experimental control.

The evaluation combines document overlap, semantic similarity, manual correctness judgments, and participant interviews. The 1,200 manually assessed document-theme pairs, double annotation, adjudication, and reported agreement provide valuable evidence beyond automated metrics.

The manuscript is generally clearly organized, and the appendices document tool operations, initialization settings, prompt templates, and LLM hardware. Separating consistency, cohesiveness, and distinctiveness exposes tradeoffs that a single aggregate score would obscure.
weaknesses: The central comparison does not establish the stated effect of collaboration modality. The introduction defines asynchronous collaboration as independent coding followed by consolidation, but Section 4 compares individual codebooks with codebooks produced by three-person synchronous teams; consolidation is omitted. Team size, access to multiple perspectives, and synchronization therefore vary together. A matched-team comparison with asynchronous consolidation, or an explicit reframing as exploratory group-versus-individual coding, is needed before the central claim supports Findings.

The statistical evidence is insufficiently justified. Each tool has only two synchronous and three asynchronous codebooks, so synchronous consistency rests on one codebook pair. Tables 1–2 report unpaired t-tests without specifying observational units, sample sizes, or treatment of dependencies among themes and comparisons sharing codebooks. Treating these observations as independent would risk pseudoreplication. Participant reuse, allocation, session order, and time budgets are also unclear. Analysis should respect these dependencies, report uncertainty, and avoid treating 'near statistically significant' results as positive evidence.

The correctness results have a concrete reporting inconsistency. Figure 4 labels the metric as F1, but Section 5 describes checking assigned document-theme pairs without defining precision, recall, or aggregation. Moreover, the claim that asynchronous operation improves topic-model correctness conflicts with the plotted pattern: asynchronous coding is higher only in the closest quartile, synchronous coding is higher in the next two cumulative subsets, and both reach approximately 0.50 overall. The metric and interpretation need correction, with uncertainty estimates.

The proposed evaluation framework needs more precise specification and validation. Maximum-similarity matching does not clearly specify directionality, one-to-one constraints, or aggregation when codebooks contain different numbers of themes. Theme counts and size distributions are missing, making granularity effects difficult to assess. Selecting the closest 25% of documents also favors cohesion by construction. Additionally, Appendix D reports invalid LLM labels for 0.7–16.1% of documents, but their treatment in quality estimates is unclear; coverage and correctness should be reported together.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the claim that all necessary information is supplied. The manuscript promises code and annotation outputs without providing an artifact link. Important missing details include the SBERT checkpoint, final codebooks, selected prompt for each session, LLM decoding settings, and manual-evaluation instructions. These affect the reported measurements and cannot all be reconstructed from the cited systems.

Several conclusions exceed the experimental scope. One English Twitter dataset and one implementation per system family support a bounded case study. They do not establish that interaction bandwidth explains collaboration benefits, because supervision, interfaces, and modeling choices also differ. Similarly, the expense and reliability of one Llama 3.2 3B-Instruct prompting configuration do not establish general limitations of LLM-based coding. These interpretations should be presented as hypotheses or restricted to the tested configurations.

The interview findings are insufficiently documented to substantiate comparative claims such as asynchronous coders being more likely to notice tool inadequacies. Appendix C acknowledges missing interviews and different interview formats across conditions, but gives no completion counts, analysis procedure, or distribution of supporting responses. The qualitative observations are useful, but currently offer limited independent confirmation of the quantitative conclusions.
